newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Houston Industries wins Colombian plant.
newsitem.headline: Houston Industries wins Colombian plant.

text.p: Houston Industries of the United States placed a winning $535 million bid on Friday for the government's 56.7 percent stake in Empresas de Energia del Pacifico (EPSA), the leading power company in southwest Colombia, government officials said.

Juan Fernando Bonilla, head of Colombia's power plant privatization program, told Reuters that the sale price was 90 percent higher than the minimum price tag the government had set for its share in EPSA and called the deal a great success.
Houston Industries is a subsidiary of Houston Light and Power, which Bonilla described as the leading power company in Texas.

Its bid beat out a $490 million offer from a Spanish consortium, led by Empresa Nacional de Electricidad (Endesa SA) and Hiberdrola, and a $440 million joint offer from Chile's Empresa Nacional de Electricidad (Endesa SA) and Colombia's Corporacion Financiera del Valle (Corfivalle).

Epsa has an installed capacity of 900 megawatts and generates and distributes electricity throughout Valle de Caucua province, one of Colombia's leading industrial hubs and an area seen as having enormous growth potential.
